_what: Seven Days to the Wolves — the whole programme, assembled from its acts. THE RUNNING ORDER IS CANONICAL and settled by the owner on 2026-08-12: intro (I) -> endlessformsmostbeautiful (II) -> mrbobbytables (III) -> kat (IV) -> nat (V) -> 7daystothewolves (VI) -> europa (VII) -> credits (VIII). docs/running-order.md is the source of truth for it; this file executes it.

_acts.0: PROLOGUE -- the main title sequence, and THE ONE ENTRY WITH NO NUMERAL. The eight act numerals are load-bearing (AGENTS.md: 'III is mrbobbytables permanently'), so a cold open in front of act I is numbered outside them rather than by renumbering everything behind it. Like act VIII it carries NO SLIDE AND NO CHAPTER MARKER: chapters() derives markers from slides, and a card announcing the main title sequence would step on the main title sequence. Picture is Nightwish's official 'Perfume Of The Timeless' music video -- see the rights note in music/bed_perfume_of_the_timeless.json, and stories/megacut/delivery.json for why it has no social copy.
_acts.I: intro — the Into the Light opener, six Guardians plated, with the title cover (wolves.jpg) covering source 24.5 - 38.
_acts.II: endlessformsmostbeautiful — delivered and credited, in the programme. Five unbroken runs of the live-action trailers scored to Nightwish's Endless Forms Most Beautiful (instrumental); The Long Walk inside them. See docs/cuts/02-endless-forms-most-beautiful.md. Its picture is a fan compilation (same provenance question as act VI, #55).
_acts.III: mrbobbytables — the August 2026 contributors piece, cut from the Curse of Osiris opening cinematic. Owner-named and owner-placed. He calls it PARTIALLY COMPLETE, so it is placed as-is and will be replaced by its finished version.
_acts.IV: kat — Kat Cosgrove's Guardian intro, behind the owner-authored BIAS FOR ACTION slide.
_acts.V: nat — Natali Vlatko's Guardian arrival, behind the same authorisation slide retitled WRONG PLACE, WRONG TIME, RIGHT ATTITUDE.
_acts.VI: 7daystothewolves — the musical. Editorial pass, delivered for review, not approved: provenance is unresolved (issue #55). Its tail plates the Cayde-6 reveal and three gold credits.
_acts.VIII: credits — the cast, 454 contributors across four projects, the comic-cover reveal at :22 and the Project Bluefin wordmark. The act that makes this the feature rather than seven eighths of it (#51).

_audio: Every act carries its own audio, unprocessed: no normaliser, no limiter, no EQ. The programme is 48 kHz STEREO because that is what the masters are -- every -hq master in Prod is stereo FLAC. The older, now-retired UPLOAD copies were AAC 5.1, but that 5.1 was the same two channels plus a derived LFE (FC/BL/BR digital silence), added by each cut's own run script. Upmixing here to recreate it would be assembly inventing a soundfield, which the audio tenet forbids; if 5.1 delivery is wanted, it belongs in the per-cut scripts that already do it. Only the six act slides are silent; a bed under them is a licensing decision.
_transitions: Issue #105, measured on v0.6 with tools/transitions.py (all times programme clock): every act entered DRY out of the slides' digital silence (4-14 s of -inf per join), the worst being act VII at -15.3 dB one second after the slide, and acts I and III ended HOT against the silence (-24.4 and -14.8 dB in their last second). The treatment below is explicit afade shapes, stated here so they are reproducible: fade_in 2.0 s on every act that starts behind a slide, fade_out 2.0 s on the acts whose tails do not already fade (I, III, V) and 3.0 s on act VII so the programme lands rather than stops. Acts II and VI fade themselves out (measured -96.7 / -90.3 dB in their last seconds) and carry no fade_out; the IV->V join is direct and continuous (-15.2 -> -11.9 dB) and carries no fade on either side. All fade times are ACT FILM time -- the clip's own clock -- so a re-order never moves them. LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): (1) whether the slides carry a bed or room tone -- a licensing decision, per the megacut skill; (2) levelling the act ENTRIES, which still differ by ~20 dB (act III at -29.5 vs act VII at -15.3) -- static gain per act is a mix decision; (3) how long the slides' silence should be -- the 15 s IV-V slide is deliberate pacing. PROLOGUE JOIN, measured 2026-08-14 on the built act rather than assumed: the prologue's own tail runs -28.3 -> -34.8 -> -58.7 dB RMS across its last three seconds (the song fading under the bridge from 93.000), and act I opens at digital silence (-127 dB) climbing through -30 to -18 dB. So the join needs NO fade on either side and carries none: the prologue fades itself out, exactly as acts II and VI do, and act I's own quiet opening picks it up. A fade_out here would double the taper on a fade the act already performs. ONE EDITORIAL FINDING, LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): the bridge exists because the owner asked for the wallpaper to 'replace the black part', and act I's 5 s silent slide immediately after it puts a black part back. It reads as a continuous darkening today -- night fades to black and the slide rises out of the same darkness, which is how a title sequence normally hands to act one -- but if the intent was for the wallpaper to hand STRAIGHT into a film, the fix is to drop or restyle act I's slide, and a slide is the one thing this show gives every act. Not changed unilaterally.

The retired ~/Videos/UPLOAD staging folder held lossy copies of the same cuts and is NOT what this reads; its removal is issue #81. Act VII's master was re-rendered 2026-08-13 under the new master gate (tools/peaks.py trim, #130) and now measures -1.1 dBTP, inside the -0.9..-1.1 band -- the +0.3 dBTP clip of #82 is fixed in the delivered file; the issue stays open for its owner to close.

items._trim: Owner 2026-08-14: 'when the song ends we want to go right into the next song, cut out the comic and fade so it goes right from wolves to this song.' Both things they asked to remove start on the SAME measured frame: 431.267 is act VI's last shot change, the comic cover ('SEVEN DAYS TO THE WOLVES / THE FIGHT FOR FREEDOM BEGINS!') comes up on it and holds 12.2 s to the end, and the song's fade-out begins on it too -- full level right up to 431.267 (-12.6 dB), then -13.9, -16.2, -26.3, -46.4 and silence by 441. So one cut removes the comic AND the fade, and the act now ends on the song's last full bar. The owner said 23:55; the measured frame is 23:59.5, and it is the frame their description names.
items._keeps_every_credit: The tail plates end at act-film 409.669 (Cayde-6 reveal 393.511, the narration, then Kelsey Hightower, Brian Ketelsen and Angie Jones). The cut is 21.6 s after the last of them, so NOTHING that credits a real person is lost -- checked before cutting, because a dropped credit is not recoverable by a revert.
items._cover_now_happens_once: The comic cover was already act VIII's reveal (#178 took it off the end of act VII for exactly this reason). Removing it here means the programme plays it once, where it lands.
items._plates: Act VI carries stories/06-wolves-cayde-plates.json burned in (tools/plate.py burn --fit-picture). Prod holds ONE file per act, hardlinked to its project master, so Prod/06 -> ~/Videos/wolves-musical/wolves-7days-plated-master-v2.mp4. The UN-PLATED v2 master is kept beside it as wolves-7days-master-v2.mp4, because burning is not idempotent: a re-burn starts from the clean file and never stacks a second card on the first. v2 re-burned the tail plates at +10.811 s film time (the manifest's _shifted records it) and the act runs 443.5 s, so slide VII and act VII move +10.811 s of programme time. THE ACT'S OWN FILE IS NOT RE-RENDERED by the trim above -- the programme ends it early, so act VI in Prod/ is untouched.

items.label: Act VII — Europa Director's Cut (no slide: a quick cut off movement 4)
items._no_slide: Owner 2026-08-14: 'get rid of the title slide.' Act VII is now the SECOND act with no slide, after act VIII -- and like act VIII that also costs it its CHAPTER MARKER, because chapters() derives markers from slides. That is a real consequence of the instruction, recorded rather than worked around: the published list is six entries now, not seven. fade_in is 0.0 so nothing eases in front of the cut.
items._shorter_tail: fade_out 3.0 -> 1.5. Europa's picture already fades to black over its own last half second, and movement 5 opens on a dark Earth limb that holds 3.5 s before the sun breaks. Three seconds of audio fade on top of that made roughly four seconds of nothing across the join.

items._no_fade_in: Owner 2026-08-14: '27:03 transition needs a dramatic analysis, very close.' Measured what is actually there: Europa ends on the Europa/Jupiter vista behind the KubeCon card and fades to black over its last half second; movement 5 then opens on a DARK EARTH LIMB (Y~24) that holds 3.504 s before the sun bursts over the curve (Y jumps to 93), then an ice plume at 4.505, and at 6.506 -- programme 27:02.3, the frame the owner marked -- the cut to the body sinking through deep blue water. Vertical motion was measured on both sides and there is NO pan: the join is dark-to-dark, not a tilt. So the problem was never the frame, it was that a 2.0 s fade IN under an already near-black 3.5 s shot, coming off a 3.0 s fade OUT, made about four seconds of nothing exactly where the film wants to hold its breath. Dropping the fade puts the song in at full level on the cut, so the dark limb becomes a held breath with music under it and the sunrise lands as the payoff.
items._still_open: If it still plays slack, the one-number alternative is to start movement 5 at the SUNRISE -- source 393.560 is a measured shot change -- so Europa's black cuts straight to the sun breaking. It is not taken here because it would open a 3.76 s hole in the song, and the thread being gapless is the whole idea. Closing that hole means extending movement 4 to 393.560, which changes the 25:13 cut the owner has already called awesome. Owner's call: #192.
items.label: Perfume, movement 5 — source 389.800 -> 507.021 (EOF), Europa into the credits
items._thread: Movement 5 of 5, and the end of the song. The owner asked to 'match the transition panning up from laura after europa'. MEASURED, AND THE PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE: there is no pan on either side. Europa's tail is the Europa/Jupiter vista behind the KubeCon card, fading to black, and movement 5 opens on a static dark Earth limb -- vertical displacement is 0 px across both, by row-profile correlation. What the join actually is, and what it is good at, is dark-to-dark: one world in space goes out, another comes up, and 3.5 s later the sun breaks over it. Act VII is never shortened to make anything fit (#178).
items._moves_the_ambush: This changes what act VIII comes out of. The credits carry no slide and no marker because 'Europa fades to black on its own tail and the drum smash lands on the next frame' -- the smash now lands off the end of a DIFFERENT song, and the source's last shot is HELD (luma ~32), not black. The 1.5 s fade_out lets the song land rather than be chopped; the picture is deliberately left un-faded, because these movements are rendered clean for the dinosaur pass and a burned dip would have to be un-baked later. TODO(owner): whether the two pieces of music collide, and whether the ambush wants black in front of it after all.

items.label: Act VIII — Credits
items._what: NO ACT SLIDE, by owner instruction: 'no credits slide, go right to the metal ... it should surprise the viewer.' Every other act is announced by a card; this one is not. Europa fades to black on its own tail and the drum smash lands on the next frame. The missing slide also removes act VIII's CHAPTER MARKER -- chapters() derives them from slides -- and that is the point rather than a side effect: a 'VIII. Credits' entry on the scrub bar would spoil the same surprise the cut is built to land. fade_in is 0.0 so nothing eases in front of the smash.

_chapters: Each act slide carries the audience-facing `chapter` title; `python3 tools/megacut.py <plan> --chapters` derives the timestamps from this plan's own clock, so the markers can never drift from the running order. The numeral is part of the title because the show is told in numbered acts. Act VIII has no slide, so it has no marker -- that is the ambush working as designed. AS OF v2.1 ACT VII HAS NONE EITHER: the owner asked for its title slide to go so movement 4 could hard-cut into Europa, and the marker went with the slide. Six published entries, not eight. If Europa should keep a scrub-bar entry without a card in front of it, chapters() would need to read a `chapter` off the CLIP -- a change nobody has asked for yet.
_version: v2.1 -- THE OWNER'S JOIN PASS on v2.0, four notes taken while watching. (1) Act VI is CUT AT 431.267, its last shot change: the comic cover and the song's fade-out both start on that frame, so one cut removes both and the act ends on a full bar -- every tail credit survives, the last of them 21.6 s earlier. (2) Act VI -> movement 4 and (3) movement 4 -> act VII are now HARD, and act VII's title slide is gone, which also costs act VII its chapter marker (chapters() derives them from slides), leaving six published entries. (4) The audio dips were pulled out of the two joins where the picture was already doing the work: act III's white-out into movement 3, and Europa's black into movement 5's dark Earth limb. Nothing was re-rendered -- act VI's file in Prod/ is untouched and the cut lives in this plan, which is what `trim_to` is for. 32:40.249 -> 32:23.016.
